newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares inch lower on China Marine.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares inch lower on China Marine.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Wednesday due in part to a fall in China Marine on profit-taking by institutions, brokers said.
The B share index shed 0.29 points, or 0.32 percent, to 89.56, with turnover rising to HK$21.65 million from HK$12.95 million on Tuesday.

China Marine sank HK$0.12 to HK$6.08 on the session's heaviest trade of 1.87 million shares. The counter had gained sharply since September and its fall on Wednesday was due to profit-taking by overseas institutions, an analyst at one Chinese brokerage said.
Light speculative selling of a handful of issues also pushed down the index, brokers said.
Shenzhen Textile, the biggest loser, fell HK$0.10, or 5.56 percent, to HK$1.70 on thin trade of 2,700 shares.
Shenzhen Properties dipped HK$0.12, or 4.58 percent, to HK$2.50 in trading of 45,000 shares.

Chiwan Wharf slipped HK$0.05 to HK$3.30, with volume rising to 544,100 shares. Beverage maker Shenbao was the strongest performer on speculative buying, brokers said. It gained HK$0.10, or 4.65 percent, to HK$2.25 with just 3,000 shares changing hands.
Dadonghai rallied HK$0.01 to HK$1.32 on the session's second most active trade of 1.54 million shares.

The A share market tumbled on Wednesday on market talk that securities regulators have launched an investigation into brokerages that illegally provided credit to their clients to trade stocks, brokers said. Officials declined to comment. Profit-taking exacerbated the retreat, they added.

The A share index fell 9.28 points, or 2.41 percent, to 376.43, with turnover falling to 6.83 billion yuan from 9.59 billion on Tuesday. The composite index fell 8.39 points, or 2.34 percent, to 350.57.
Xiamen Haifa was the worst performer, down 0.69 yuan, or 7.26 percent, to 8.81 yuan.
Port operator Beihai Xinli followed with a fall of 0.79 yuan, or 7.00 percent, to 10.49 yuan.
